notes: Page 2 only shows the minifigure being assembled (helmet, visor, head, torso with arms and hands, legs). None of these pieces are in the provided parts list or catalogue, so no nodes or edges were added for this page.
Step 2 shows the 2x6 plate upside down; the two round 2x2 plates attach to its underside (studs into the plate's anti-studs), one at each end. Each round plate gets one joined edge between the pair.
Round plate positions assumed at columns 1-2 and 5-6 of the plate.

Step 3: the two wheel-holder plates are attached to the outward-facing sides of the round plates, with the 2x6 plate still upside down. The left one is already shown fitted and the right one is being added; both are recorded here.
The 4600 is only joined to its round plate (one edge per pair), not to the 2x6 plate.

Step 4: the chassis is flipped so the stud side of the 2x6 plate faces up, with the round plates and wheel holders underneath. Each end gets a side-handle plate across the end column and a light grey 1x2 plate beside it.
Exact stud positions are inferred from a small, ambiguous illustration. The side-handle plates are assumed to sit at the outermost columns (1 and 6), with the 1x2 plates at columns 2 and 5.

Step 5: an orange mudguard covers the 2x2 area at each end of the chassis. It sits on the side-handle plate and the 1x2 plate at that end. The left mudguard is already shown fitted and the right one is being added; both are recorded here.
Each mudguard bridges two parts, so it gets two joined edges. The anti-stud ports used are the central ones, assumed from orientation.

Step 6: the picture shows two white jumper plates already on the left mudguard (b10), and a white grille tile already on the right mudguard (b11). A third white jumper is being added next to the grille tile. All four pieces are recorded here.
The grille tile is not shown being added in any step I could see. I assumed it sits on the right mudguard, which is how it is drawn.
Each jumper or tile is joined to its mudguard with one edge for the pair. Exact stud positions are inferred.
Step 7: a trans-yellow cheese slope goes on the left white jumper, and a dark grey clip tile sits on the exposed stud of the 2x6 plate beside the left mudguard.
The illustration is small. The jumper chosen for the slope (b12) and the plate stud for the clip tile (stud.1.3) are assumed.
Step 8: the antenna goes on the right white jumper stud. The blue flag clips onto the antenna shaft, shown in the inset. The handlebars go onto the clip tile.
The antenna has no port for the shaft in the catalogue, so the flag's edge to the antenna has a null port on that side.
Step 9: four wheels, each a white rim pressed into a black tyre. Each wheel is pushed onto a pin of a wheel-holder plate. Copies 1 and 2 go on b4 and copies 3 and 4 on b5.
The minifigure on the finished model is not in the parts list, so it is not recorded. Which axle-hole port is which pin is assumed.
